archetype: Mardu Vampire ARISTOCRATS-MIDRANGE on an eminence chassis — v1.1.1 (decklist sha 7be137d0…, sleeved 2026-09-16 after branch elenda-v1 merged). The pilot's stated direction (quiver inventory, 2026-09-16) is two lines: go wide with tokens, and funnel the value into a few bigger Vampires; lifegain-into-drain as a THEME, with the lifegain infinite deliberately out. Edgar Markov's eminence mints a 1/1 Vampire on every Vampire spell from the command zone (stacks 002/010 checker-passed), three replacement doublers multiply it (1→4 with two, 1→8 with three, all six orders — stack 010), and eight sacrifice outlets by role (deck-facts sac-outlet 8: Altar of Dementia, Ashnod's Altar, Bloodflow Connoisseur, Indulgent Aristocrat, Master of Dark Rites, Viscera Seer, Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter, Yahenni, Undying Partisan — seven of them cost no mana) convert the bodies into counters, cards and life loss. The two swaps are both DEATH PAYOFFS: Elenda, the Dusk Rose (+1/+1 per other death, dies into X lifelink Vampires — the hinge between the two lines, since she is the 'big Vampire' that pays out as 'go wide') and Blade of the Bloodchief (two counters per death on an equipped Vampire) replace Immersturm Predator and Unbounded Potential. What the artifacts say that the direction does not: deck-facts and engine-facts both list TWO fully-contained two-card infinites — Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose, and with Sanguine Bond — and both are checker-passed (stacks 004, 006). Exquisite Blood left the 99; Conqueror is its text on a body. The 'infinite is OUT' decision is not enacted in the list, and this frame carries the loop as present, verified and subordinate-by-choice rather than absent.

role_assignment.default_role: BEATDOWN — assigned per seat, and delivered by drain more than by clock. strategy:whos-the-beatdown: 'the roles are set by matchup and game state, not your deck's label' and, in a pod, 'role is seat-relative — you can be the beatdown against one opponent and the control against another in the same turn cycle; assign per-threat, not per-game'. The pilot calls this the fastest deck in the quiver and the artifacts agree it is fast at DEVELOPING, not at killing: goldfish (seed 42, 10,000 games, model 5496ad1975b1, this sha) draws a castable Vampire in 95.0% of games at mean turn 2.22, has 7.69 bodies at turn 6, and kills one unblocked opponent by turn 8 in 70.4% (median kill turn 8, mean 7.96) — with no blockers, no interaction and DEATH-TRIGGERED DRAIN NOT MODELLED (goldfish meta: 'the largest known gap here'). Forge has never run this sha; on v1.1.0 against standard-v3 the seat's median first attack was global turn 12 (n=57) and 13 (n=38), i.e. roughly its own turn 6-7, with 19/46 decided (0.413) and 8/27 (0.296) — and 14 of 60 and 13 of 40 games clocked out. So the metagame-clock correction reads as an instruction, not a warning: 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan and aggro must instead compress the game before the table's late game arrives' (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). What compresses is the drain — strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry: 'wide alpha strikes, loops, commander-damage kills, and each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale' — which is why Cruel Celebrant (each opponent) is deployed before Blood Artist (one target player), and why Sanctum Seeker's attack trigger under Bloodletter (stack 003) is the fastest verified kill in the 99.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: strategy:pivot-point: 'The pivot is usually triggered by a concrete event — a resolved engine, a wrath, a key removal spell spent, a life total crossing a clock threshold. Plan for it before it happens: hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after'. This list's concrete events, in the order they usually arrive: (1) a free outlet AND a death payoff both on the battlefield — an outlet is drawn in 72.3% of goldfish games (59.3% by turn 6), a death drain in 37.2% (25.2% by turn 6), and nothing measures the PAIR, so the trigger is the board, not a rate; from here every eminence token is a card, a counter or a point of drain rather than an attacker. (2) Elenda, the Dusk Rose at four or more power with a doubler out — she is the moment the 'few big Vampires' line converts back into the 'go wide' line at a rate the table cannot block, and she is the sacrifice you make ON PURPOSE the turn a wrath is coming (needs a stack scenario for the exact count). (3) Bloodletter of Aclazotz resolving with Sanctum Seeker or a drain body already out (stack 003) — assembled in only 4.1% of goldfish games (1.6% by turn 6), so it is a windfall, not a plan. (4) Bloodthirsty Conqueror resolving with Vito or Sanguine Bond — the verified loop (stacks 004, 006), 7.8% assembled (3.4% by turn 6); the pilot has said this is not the deck's plan, and the frame respects that, but the board does not know it: with Conqueror, Vito and any death drain out, the next death IS the loop. Commit only when the attempt cannot be profitably answered: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing' (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). Log 005 is the counter-example — Elspeth exposed, tempo pushed, planeswalker taken, Purphoros pings closed — and strategy:resource-hedging's rule for that spot is 'hedge from ahead, gamble from behind … deploy only what you need, simplify, bank protection'. The protection that covers Elspeth is enumerated: Boros Charm ('Permanents you control gain indestructible') and Teferi's Protection (everything phases out) — Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will name CREATURES and do not reach her; Deflecting Swat retargets a spell or ability, so it stops a targeted removal spell but not an attack.

engines.engine: Eminence: 'Whenever you cast another Vampire spell, if Edgar is in the command zone or on the battlefield, create a 1/1 black Vampire creature token'. Ignition is free, undrawable and cannot be interacted with — checker-passed stack 010 resolves it with Edgar NEVER having entered the battlefield. Low commander dependence is measured, not asserted: Edgar is cast by turn 6 in 60.3% of goldfish games (mean 6.32, median 6) and no verified kill route needs him on the battlefield; his attack trigger ('put a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire you control') is a bonus to the counters line, not its engine. Log 001's own lesson stands: make casting him a decision from the first affordable turn.
engines.evidence: oracle text + verified stacks 002 and 010 + goldfish_metrics.commander (sha 7be137d0)

engines.engine: Token multiplication with Mondrak, Glory Dominus and Elspeth, Storm Slayer: three replacement effects stacking multiplicatively, 1→2→4→8 under all six orders (stack 010). A multiplier is drawn in 67.9% of goldfish games (51.8% by turn 6). Under this frame the multiplier's job is FODDER and, since v1.1.1, Elenda's payout: her death trigger creates tokens 'under your control', so the same replacement effects should apply to her X — the count is a candidate line until a stack says so. model-coverage flags all three doublers DARK on the treasure channel, which is off for this deck; read their goldfish value as a floor.
engines.evidence: oracle text + verified stacks 002, 010 + goldfish target 'A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn' 0.679 + model-coverage (treasure channel off)

engines.engine: The conversion layer: eight sacrifice outlets by role (deck-facts sac-outlet 8) — Altar of Dementia, Ashnod's Altar, Bloodflow Connoisseur, Indulgent Aristocrat, Master of Dark Rites, Viscera Seer, Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter, Yahenni, Undying Partisan — of which seven cost no mana (Indulgent Aristocrat bills {2}; Master of Dark Rites and Ashnod's Altar MAKE mana, the Rites' restricted to Vampire/Cleric/Demon SPELLS per deck-facts' restricted_mana note). A free outlet is drawn in 72.3% of goldfish games at mean turn 3.16, and the goldfish now sacrifices (mean 2.93 sacrifices by turn 10, sac_cap_hit_rate 0.0) — but Forge does not: across every Forge record on v1.1.0, Viscera Seer was cast 0 times and Altar of Dementia cast 0 times, Ashnod's Altar activated 0, so every Forge rate on this deck is a floor on the conversion stage exactly as CLAUDE.md warns. The counts in the prose disagree: the pilot's prompt says six outlets, the branch text says nine (it counted Immersturm Predator, now out); deck-facts says eight and this frame uses eight.
engines.evidence: deck-facts roles (sac-outlet 8, sac-cost 8) + oracle text + goldfish target 0.723 + Forge engine_casts on v1.1.0 (2026-09-06, 09-09, 09-11)

engines.engine: NEW in v1.1.1, the hinge between the pilot's two lines. 'Whenever another creature dies, put a +1/+1 counter on Elenda' makes her grow on every death at the table, yours or theirs — every outlet activation, every chump, every opposing wipe feeds her — and 'When Elenda dies, create X 1/1 white Vampire creature tokens with lifelink, where X is Elenda's power' converts that size back into width, lifelink, and (with Vito or Sanguine Bond) drain. She is also the biggest POWER store for the two outlets that read power: Vish Kal ('Put X +1/+1 counters on Vish Kal, where X is the sacrificed creature's power') and Altar of Dementia ('mills cards equal to the sacrificed creature's power'). strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's threat rule is the reason she fits: 'board quality beats board quantity (Walser), because a single scaling permanent out-values a fair board against three players'. The goldfish cannot see her: model-coverage lists her DARK on the drain channel (model_drain is off for this deck), and the branch objective was a CONTROL (kill_by_8 0.701 vs the champion's 0.704) precisely because nothing in the model prices a death payoff. Every number about her is therefore a candidate line.
engines.evidence: oracle text + branch elenda-v1 (objective = control, reading 0.701) + model-coverage (DARK, drain channel off)

engines.engine: NEW in v1.1.1: 'Whenever a creature dies, put a +1/+1 counter on equipped creature. If equipped creature is a Vampire, put two +1/+1 counters on it instead' for {1} plus equip {1}. Two counters per death on any Vampire, repeatable — the branch's stated reason was 'a repeatable counter engine for the one-shot' (Unbounded Potential). On a lifelinker (Nighthawk Scavenger, Elenda, Vampire of the Dire Moon, Vampire Cutthroat, Gifted Aetherborn, Indulgent Aristocrat, Vish Kal, The Haunt of Hightower — the eight printed-lifelink bodies, enumerated from cards.json) each death adds two to the next lifelink hit and so to the next Vito or Sanguine Bond trigger. It is the cheapest expression of the 'funnel value into a few bigger Vampires' line and it composes with Cordial Vampire (one counter on EVERY Vampire per death) and Elenda (one on herself) to three counters per death on the equipped Elenda.

Deaths into SIZE across the whole board: 'Whenever this creature or another creature dies, put a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire you control'. With Blade of the Bloodchief and Elenda it is the counters line's third engine; buff:counters is the largest role class in the deck (15 copies). This is the mechanical answer to the 400-game Forge finding on v1.0.0 that 1/1 tokens do not connect (combat damage to players 29.07→18.20 in the refactor) — the deck buys a few large bodies with deaths instead of many medium ones with tokens.
engines.evidence: oracle text + deck-facts roles (buff:counters 15) + captain's log 003 (the direction change)

engines.engine: Deaths and entries into CARDS: Crossway Troublemakers ('Whenever a Vampire you control dies, you may pay 2 life. If you do, draw a card'), High-Society Hunter ('Whenever another NONTOKEN creature dies, draw a card' — blind to every eminence token and to Elenda's tokens), Liliana, Dreadhorde General ('Whenever a creature you control dies, draw a card'), Skullclamp, plus the entry draw of Welcoming Vampire and Caretaker's Talent (both once per turn) and Champion of Dusk, Bloodtracker, Preacher of the Schism, Night's Whisper, Castle Locthwain. A draw engine is drawn in 83.5% of goldfish games (72.6% by turn 6, mean turn 2.62) — the healthiest component in the brief and the direct fix for the cause code on logs 002 and 003 ('ran out of steam'). Read the model's caveat with it: 16 cards draw, 6 are modelled, and the ten in goldfish meta draw_not_modelled include every death-triggered one, so mean extra cards drawn (2.49 by turn 10) is a floor. deck-audit reads card-advantage UNDER (7 vs 10) with nine possibly-uncounted cards named. strategy:card-advantage: 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage'.
engines.evidence: oracle text + goldfish target 0.835 + goldfish meta card_advantage (6 of 16 modelled) + deck-audit card-advantage axis

engines.engine: Death drain with Blood Artist. The asymmetry decides deployment order: Cruel Celebrant hits 'each opponent', Blood Artist 'target player' — strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry: 'effects that tax or drain every opponent at once'. Log 002 is the measured case on the old list: a wipe with Blood Artist and Bloodthirsty Conqueror out killed eleven creatures and took every opponent for 11. This is the stage that makes a sweeper the deck's best turn rather than its worst, and it is the stage the goldfish explicitly does not model ('DEATH-TRIGGERED DRAIN IS NOT MODELLED AND IS THE LARGEST KNOWN GAP HERE'). A death drain is drawn in 37.2% of games (25.2% by turn 6).
engines.evidence: oracle text + goldfish target 0.372 + goldfish meta model_assumptions + captain's log 002

engines.engine: The lifegain-to-drain converter and the deck's ONLY two-card infinites, verified: Conqueror + Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose (stack 004) and Conqueror + Sanguine Bond (stack 006), both 'Infinite lifeloss' per combo_details (bracket 3, popularity 64,824 and 54,630), both fully contained per deck-facts. Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles any opponent's life loss on your turn (stack 003 with Sanctum Seeker; the 'THE DRAIN DOUBLER' target, 4.1% assembled). deck-audit prices Conqueror and Bloodletter as the deck's two single points of failure. The pilot's direction says the lifegain infinite is OUT and drain is a theme, not a combo; the 99 says otherwise, and this frame reports the disagreement rather than resolving it. Practically: with Conqueror and either half on the battlefield, ANY lifegain event — a lifelink hit, a Celebrant trigger, Elenda's tokens connecting — starts the loop, so 'not the plan' has to be a play decision every turn those pieces coexist, and log 004's open question (would the pilot's proposed pod norm against two-card infinites disarm his own proven kills?) is still the live one.
engines.evidence: deck-facts combos (2 contained, 2 two-card infinites) + engine-facts candidate_lines + verified stacks 003, 004, 006 + deck-audit single_points_of_failure

candidate_missing_lines.title: Elenda under the doublers: sacrifice a 6-power Elenda to Viscera Seer with Anointed Procession and Mondrak out — how many lifelink Vampires, is X read from last-known power, and do Cordial Vampire / Blade / Elenda's own trigger fire for the tokens' later deaths?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: Elenda's death trigger creates 'X 1/1 white Vampire creature tokens with lifelink, where X is Elenda's power', tokens created 'under your control', which is the wording the two doublers replace; stack 010 established the replacement-effect arithmetic for eminence tokens (1→4 with two doublers) but never for a death trigger whose X depends on the dead creature's last-known power. This is the exact mechanism the branch was merged for and the pilot's stated hinge between 'a few big Vampires' and 'go wide'; no artifact measures it (goldfish: model_drain off, Elenda DARK).

candidate_missing_lines.title: Lifelink tokens as a drain: eight lifelink Vampires connect with Vito and Bloodletter out — one Vito trigger per creature or one per combat, and what does each opponent lose?
cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Vito reads 'Whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life'; lifelink from several sources dealing combat damage simultaneously is one damage event but each source's lifelink is its own gain — whether that is one trigger or eight decides whether Vito can split the drain across seats, and Bloodletter's 'twice that much life' applies per loss on your turn. This is the pilot's stated 'feeding Vito and Sanguine Bond' and no stack has priced it.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The infinite that fires by accident: Conqueror, Vito and Cruel Celebrant on the battlefield, one creature dies — is the loop already running, and can the pilot decline it?
cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stacks 004 and 006 verified the loop from a deliberate 3-life seed. The pilot's direction is that the infinite is not the plan, but Celebrant's death trigger is a lifegain event and Vito's and Conqueror's triggers are mandatory ('target opponent loses that much life', 'you gain that much life'), so a routine sacrifice with all three out may be the loop whether intended or not. The answer decides whether 'theme, not combo' is a play decision or a list decision.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Which of the 99 removes Purphoros, God of the Forge: does Stroke of Midnight's 'destroy' fail against indestructible, does Liliana's −4 miss a non-creature Purphoros, and does Deflecting Swat have a target to move?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Log 005 lost to Purphoros ETB pings and asks for 'targeted disruption in white'. Enumerated from cards.json over deck-audit's 11 interactive copies: only Despark ('Exile target permanent with mana value 4 or greater') and Anguished Unmaking ('Exile target nonland permanent') exile a noncreature indestructible permanent; Path to Exile, Winds of Abandon, Elspeth −3 and Vish Kal want a creature; Stroke of Midnight destroys. The goldfish target 'An answer to a noncreature permanent drawn' (49.3%, 34.8% by turn 6) counts Stroke of Midnight and so overstates the answer rate against an indestructible target. A stack settles the two-card figure before diagnose sizes a swap.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The v1.1.0 draw loop, still unproven: sacrifice N eminence tokens to a free outlet with Crossway Troublemakers and High-Society Hunter out — how many cards, at what life, and does the Hunter see any of them?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Carried from the previous frame, still without a stack. Crossway Troublemakers reads 'Whenever a Vampire you control dies, you may pay 2 life. If you do, draw a card'; High-Society Hunter 'Whenever another nontoken creature dies, draw a card' is blind to tokens on a plain read. This is the loop the pilot ran in log 004 and the deck's central stage-to-stage arrow.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Altar of Dementia as the alternate kill: sacrifice a Cordial-grown Elenda or Vish Kal — mill count, the death drains on the way, and when the milled player actually loses
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Carried from the previous frame with Elenda replacing The Haunt of Hightower as the power store: Altar of Dementia mills 'cards equal to the sacrificed creature's power' and Elenda now carries the deck's fastest-growing power. The pilot's 28-August pivot asked for a mill dig; this is the only route in the 99 and it is unmeasured.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Vampire Socialite's sequencing rule: cast the Vampire before or after the turn's first drain?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Carried forward: Socialite reads 'As long as an opponent lost life this turn, each other Vampire you control enters with an additional +1/+1 counter on it' — a free power per token decided by play order; stacks 002 and 011 show eminence tokens entering with and without it on boards differing only in timing.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: The wipe is your engine, and v1.1.1 made it more so: strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math says 'assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain' and to 'buy resilience instead of restraint where you can — high toughness, indestructible and regeneration, token rebuilders, threats that replace themselves'. Elenda is now a threat that replaces herself WITH the wipe (X lifelink Vampires on death), the death payoffs (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant, Cordial Vampire, Crossway Troublemakers, High-Society Hunter, Liliana, Skullclamp, Blade of the Bloodchief) make a resolved sweeper drain the table and refill your hand, and eminence rebuilds from a zone no sweeper touches. Log 002 measured it: eleven deaths, 11 off every opponent. Still deploy in waves — 'redeploy worst-first, keeping the best threat in hand for their second sweeper' — and know what the insurance does NOT reach: Anointed Procession, Sanguine Bond, Caretaker's Talent and Blade of the Bloodchief are noncreature, so only Teferi's Protection and Boros Charm cover them; Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will cover creatures only. Against the counterspell seat (log 001 lost two key spells to Tom) the rule is strategy:tempo.sequencing: 'strike in the window when opponents are tapped out and cannot respond' and 'prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent' — which this deck can do only with its instants; a Champion of Dusk into open blue mana is the spot the log names.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: You are the profile the taxes are printed against: strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial — 'Decks built on many cheap spells per turn are hit hardest: taxes attack the velocity math directly, so recount your hand under the tax — a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine'. 27 of 64 nonland entries sit at mana value 2 or less and every one of them is an eminence trigger, so a tax halves the fodder as well as the casts. Role is forced — 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion' — and the outs are the 11 interactive copies deck-audit counts, of which the two catch-alls are Anguished Unmaking and Despark; breadth covers creature, artifact and enchantment and leaves graveyard and LAND uncovered (deck-audit interaction-breadth, under), so a land-based lock must be raced. Name the out early: 'the removal or velocity that breaks the piece that beats *you*, not the scariest piece'. Seven of the eight outlets cost no mana, which is the one part of the engine a tax cannot touch.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: The matchup lifegain is for. Eight printed-lifelink bodies, Elenda's token payout, Legion's Landing, Mavren Fein, Charismatic Conqueror and Preacher of the Schism all make lifelink Vampires, and with Vito or Sanguine Bond out every point gained is a point drained. strategy:life-as-resource: 'Your life total is currency, not a score. Only the last point matters' and 'its points appreciate as they dwindle, so early points are cheap and late points are priceless' — the licence for Champion of Dusk, Night's Whisper, Crossway Troublemakers, Bloodtracker and Castle Locthwain to bill you early, and the instruction to stop paying the turn a burn or drain seat is in range (log 004's own lesson, 'pay the life', is the early-turn half of this). strategy:combat-math.racing: 'you cannot race three life totals — races there are two-player subgames run while the rest of the table develops, so spend the minimum that wins yours and keep watching the other seats'. Assign per seat: beatdown against the aggro deck's life total, blockers-and-drain against the other two; a deathtouch lifelinker (Gifted Aetherborn, Vampire of the Dire Moon, Nighthawk Scavenger) is the block that pays.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: No stack interaction beyond Deflecting Swat (a retarget, not a counter), so the levers are the drain, the clock and threat perception. strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: 'deploy engines that read as defensive, sequence scary pieces after the table's removal is spent' and 'Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress'. This deck's tells are Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito, Sanguine Bond and Bloodletter — the pieces the table reads as a combo whether or not the pilot means to fire one — and a board of 1/1 lifelink tokens and a growing Elenda reads as fair. The single tutor (Vampiric Tutor) buys the missing half of whichever verified route is live, per strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors: a tutor is 'essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck' and a named card is only '7.1% of your opening seven'. Log 004 lost to a tutored two-card infinite and the pilot wants a pod norm against them; the frame's honest note is that the norm would also disarm stacks 004 and 006. Against combo the pivot-window rule inverts: strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy — 'held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now'.
matchup_frames.vs_etb_trigger_race: The predator the pilot named after log 005 (Purphoros: 'the natural predator for mid-range aggro'), and Forge agrees on v1.1.0 — the 2026-09-03 playgroup pod with purphoros-pingers seated gave this seat 4 of 38 decided games (0.105) and purphoros-pingers 19 of 38, against 0.413 and 0.296 on standard-v3 (all on v1.1.0; the current sha has no Forge record; Forge's sacrifice floor applies to every figure). A trigger-racer does not care about blockers, so 'keep blockers up' protects Elspeth, not your life total; what protects the life total is strategy:life-as-resource's switch — 'knowing when your life total has become real (combo decks in range, burn reach, lethal on board next turn) and switching from spending to defending one turn before it matters, not one after' — and strategy:threat-assessment's ranking: 'Rank threats on three axes: clock (how fast it kills you), inevitability … and interaction cost'; an enchantment that pings on every entry has the fastest clock at the table against a 40-life deck that pays life for cards, so it outranks the scariest creature. The answer set is enumerated and small: of the eleven interactive copies deck-audit counts, Despark and Anguished Unmaking are the two that exile a noncreature indestructible permanent (Stroke of Midnight destroys; the creature removal needs a creature), and Teferi's Protection buys one turn cycle ('your life total can't change'). Two copies is a 14% opening-seven proposition by the doc's own arithmetic; whether that is a swap is a diagnose question, and the stack scenario above should settle the count first. Role under this seat is beatdown by drain — your each-opponent drains and lifelink outrun a symmetric pinger only if you stop feeding it entries you do not need, which is strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's 'commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further'.

distribution_notes: Copies, not entries (deck-facts, sha 7be137d0): 100 copies across 96 entries — 36 land copies in 32 entries, 64 spells. Curve 13 / 14 / 19 / 8 / 5 / 4 / 1 across mana values 1–7, modal 3, 27 entries at mana value 2 or less. Roles (coverage 100%): threat:body 37, buff:counters 15, threat:tokens 10, sac-outlet 8, sac-cost 8, draw:engine 6, removal:spot 6, wincon:drain 6, protection:self 6, wincon:combat 4, doubler:tokens 3, tutor 1. Mondrak, Glory Dominus is the only non-Vampire creature in the 99 (enumerated over 96 entries). deck-audit against strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection's 'aggro 26-32 creatures / 5-6 removal / 34-36 lands': creatures OVER (37) and interaction OVER (11) — both deliberate — sweepers UNDER (0), card-advantage UNDER (7 vs 10, nine possibly-uncounted named), ramp UNDER (8 vs 10-12), colour-sources UNDER (B 32 vs Karsten 36, R 20 vs 22, W 24 vs 22), protection AT (7 of a 5-7 band), threat density AT (10). Mana: 54 black pips across 38 cards; on-curve with rocks B 0.855, R 0.881, W 0.927 (mana_analysis, same sha); 15 of 32 land entries enter tapped. Goldfish (seed 42, 10,000, model 5496ad1975b1): keep 81.1% of first sevens, 0.226 mulligans, 96.4% can act by turn 3, turn-3 land 91.9%, mean mana 5.59 at turn 6, bodies 7.69 at 6 and 15.8 at 10, sacrifices 2.93 by 10, extra cards 2.49 by 10 (floor: 10 draw cards unmodelled), interaction castable at turn 6 only 26.9% though in hand 88.3% — the number behind the pilot's log-002 read that 'a deck that cannot afford to hold up interaction is a deck that does not run interaction'. Diagnostic (seed 20260826): turn-2 stall 24.6% and 'worse than any tracked deck' from turn 2, missed a land drop by five 39.9%, mana 'below the fleet median' — a 36-land, 8-ramp list with 13 one-drops stalls on MANA, not on gas. Branch objective was a control: kill_by_8 0.701 on the branch against 0.704 on the champion, met, because the goldfish cannot price a death payoff. Bracket floor 4 (Optimized): Ancient Tomb, Teferi's Protection, Vampiric Tutor plus the two contained two-card infinites.
overall_assessment: This deck plays the aristocrats game on an aggro chassis, and v1.1.1 is the first list where the two lines the pilot named are the same card: Elenda grows on every death (the 'few big Vampires' line) and dies into a doubled swarm of lifelink Vampires (the 'go wide' line), while Blade of the Bloodchief turns every eminence token's death into two counters on whichever Vampire is carrying the game. strategy:critical-mass still names the ignition — a linear deck 'entirely focused on one goal or theme' whose defence is 'speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers' — but the number to know is no longer bodies; it is DEATHS CONVERTED, and nothing in the artifact set measures a body being eaten: every conversion figure (outlet 72.3%, death drain 37.2%, draw engine 83.5%) measures a card being drawn, the goldfish runs with model_drain off and eleven drain cards DARK, and Forge cast Viscera Seer zero times in 260 games. The school that justifies the whole shape is strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry — '~120 combined life behind three defenses makes incremental combat damage a losing plan' and 'each-opponent drains are the payoffs that actually scale' — with its threat corollary 'board quality beats board quantity' licensing Elenda, Vish Kal and the counters line over an army of 1/1s that the 400-game Forge record showed do not connect. The role is beatdown per seat, by drain, on a clock that develops fast (Vampire by 2.2, 7.7 bodies by turn 6) and closes slowly (goldfish median kill turn 8 with no blockers; Forge median first attack around the seat's own turn 6-7), which makes strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's 'aggro must instead compress the game before the table's late game arrives' the standing instruction and strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window the discipline: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal'. Both current-list games (004, 005) reached a winning board and lost on the close, and the pilot's own reading — tuning has moved 'from rebuild the deck to sequence and close better' — is what strategy:pivot-point says about turning the corner: 'once you stabilize, every extra passive turn is a free draw step for the opponent'. Two things the frame must say plainly. First, the artifacts and the direction disagree about the infinite: the 99 holds two checker-passed two-card loops (Conqueror with Vito, Conqueror with Sanguine Bond), the pilot says the infinite is out and drain is a theme, and no list change enacts that — so at the table 'not the plan' is a decision the pilot makes every turn those pieces coexist, and log 004's open question about the pod norm is unanswered. Second, the deck's measured weakness is mana, not gas: the diagnostic's turn-2 stall is the worst on the fleet, black is four sources short of Karsten's target, and a deck that spends every turn's mana casting Vampires holds up interaction 27% of the time at turn 6 — which is the structural half of log 005's loss (tempo pushed, planeswalker exposed) and of log 002's ('never open mana to hold up'). The strategic answer is not more interaction cards (deck-audit already reads interaction over): it is strategy:resource-hedging's 'hedge from ahead … deploy only what you need, simplify, bank protection' applied to a deck whose free protection (Flawless Maneuver, Deflecting Swat) costs nothing to hold once Edgar is out — and an honest count that only Boros Charm and Teferi's Protection reach a planeswalker.
gaps: No school for ARISTOCRATS: outlet counts, free-versus-costed outlets, the fodder-to-payoff ratio, and how many payoffs before the outlets are the bottleneck. This frame stretched strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math and strategy:card-advantage to cover a deck whose own board dying is the plan. The query 'aristocrats sacrifice outlets death triggers fodder' top-scored 0.23 against The Philosophy of Fire.

No school for TOKENS AS FUEL rather than as threats; strategy:critical-mass prices a threshold of bodies and nothing prices a token whose job is to be eaten — the distinction log 003 drew and the reason v1.0.0's 400-game Forge result did not transfer.

No school for LIFEGAIN AS AN ENGINE: lifelink density, gain-to-drain converters, and when a lifegain deck is a drain deck. strategy:life-as-resource treats life only as currency spent. The pilot's 'theme, not combo' decision has no doc line to check it against, and the best hit for 'lifegain as a win condition' was 0.47 on that section.

No section on SEQUENCING AGAINST A TRIGGER-RACER (Purphoros / Impact Tremors decks): attack it, hold back, or answer the enchantment. Log 005's open question and the punchlist both route it to research-strategy; the frame answered it from threat-assessment and life-as-resource, which is a stretch. Best hit for the phrasing was 0.41 on the interaction-suite section.

No section on PLANESWALKER PROTECTION in a creature deck — what covers a walker, at what cost to the attack, and when a walker is the engine to protect rather than the tempo to spend. Log 005's lesson ('protect the engine before pushing tempo') was grounded in strategy:pivot-point and strategy:resource-hedging, neither of which mentions walkers.

No section on TURN ORDER in a five-player pod (log 002's open question: does seat 5 compound with a mana deficit multiplicatively or additively?) — still routed to research-strategy, still unanswered; best hits were The Pivot Point and Damage Racing at 0.36-0.37.
No school for SELF-MILL / the graveyard as a resource, which the 28-August pivot asked for as a second dig; the only route in the 99 is Altar of Dementia and it is unmeasured.
No section on TYPAL DENSITY (lords against creature count against removal exposure): the query scored 0.16 and matched the mana-base section.

No section on COMMAND-ZONE ENGINES: strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance prices the recast tax, which eminence never pays; an ignition that cannot be interacted with and a commander you often do not want to cast has no theory. The pilot's 'commander dependence low' is a measured fact with no school.

MEASUREMENT gaps the orchestrator should route rather than the doc: (a) the goldfish runs this deck with model_drain OFF and eleven drain cards DARK including both new cards' payoffs (model-coverage) — switch it on and re-measure before any figure about Elenda, Vito or Sanguine Bond is read; (b) no Forge record exists on the current sha 7be137d0, and every existing record is a sacrifice floor (Viscera Seer 0 casts in every run); (c) deck-audit's archetype table has no 'aristocrats' bucket, so creatures and interaction read OVER when both counts are deliberate; (d) the three prose sources disagree on the outlet count (pilot six, branch nine, deck-facts eight) and the frame follows deck-facts.

DECISION the orchestrator must surface: the pilot's direction says the lifegain infinite is OUT, and the sleeved 99 contains two checker-passed two-card infinites (stacks 004, 006) on cards the same direction keeps as its drain theme. Either the direction means Exquisite Blood specifically (then the frame stands as written) or it means no two-card loop (then Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito or Sanguine Bond must leave and the verified kill routes change). This frame does not pick.
